A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TRELLIS/SLAT research work, with 26 complete pages including appendices A–E. Pages 2–26 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page differences are fully readable.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and generation experiments, ablations, qualitative demonstrations, and a 104-participant user study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–5, the timestep ablation in Table 7, and user-study outcomes in Table 9.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical SLAT encoding, representation-specific decoders, two-stage rectified-flow generation, training objectives, and editing procedures.

E1.justification: The four training sources, Toys4k evaluation, and AI-generated and SA-1B image-prompt scenarios are unchanged. Both versions cover the same reconstruction, text/image-to-3D generation, editing, and scene-composition tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their experiment-specific comparator sets, including CLAY for reconstruction and GaussianCube for text-to-3D. Appendix D.2 and Figure 16 retain the same Rodin Gen-1 image-to-3D comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–C retain identical training settings, rendering procedures, metrics, and user-study design. Reconstruction still evaluates 500 Toys4k objects; generation evaluation uses 1,250 Toys4k and 5,000 training-set instances.

E4.justification: The latent-size, generation-paradigm, model-size, and timestep-sampling ablations in Tables 3–5 and 7 are identical. The supplementary real-image, editing, and scene-composition demonstrations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains identical, including the aesthetic-score distributions in Figure 8 and user-study counts and percentages in Table 9. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 2 still reports Ours L text-to-3D CLIP 26.60 and DINOv2 FD 238.60; Table 9 retains preference rates of 67.1% and 94.5%.

T1.justification: The SLAT definition, flow objective, decoder and loss formulations, and metric definitions in Equations 1–14 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about generation quality, versatile output formats, fitting-free training, and tuning-free editing. Relocating the resource-availability sentence does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning two-stage generation efficiency and baked-in lighting, with the same proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware, hyperparameters, data preparation, and evaluation details are unchanged. The existing code/model/data availability statement moves from the abstract to a title footnote with the same project link; no new resource availability is documented.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and comparisons with prior research are identical. No cited works or substantive novelty-positioning statements are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 rephrases the abstract's final availability sentence as an 'Open-source project' title footnote, adds its title marker, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All subsequent wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title footnote changes first-page spacing: Figure 1 shifts slightly and the abstract and footnotes reflow. Figure content and captions are unchanged, and pages 2–26 have identical rendered layouts.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the complete scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations of v2, including the appendices. Moving the availability statement to a title footnote and adjusting first-page layout provides no meaningful net change in paper quality.
